Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 112, verses 1–4:

This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} That is, {Say}: say it with firm conviction, believing in it, knowing its meaning: {He is Allah, the One (Ahad)}; that is, oneness (uniqueness, ahadiyyah) is confined to Him. He is the One, the Singular in perfection, who possesses the Most Beautiful Names, the most perfect and sublime attributes, and the sanctified acts, having no counterpart and no like.

{2} {Allah, the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad)}; that is, the one sought in all needs. The inhabitants of the higher and lower worlds are utterly in need of Him; they ask Him for their needs and turn to Him in their affairs, because He is perfect in His attributes: the All-Knowing whose knowledge is complete, the Forbearing whose forbearance is complete, the Merciful whose mercy is complete, whose mercy encompasses everything... and likewise all His other attributes.

{3} And among His perfection is that {He neither begets nor is born}, because of the completeness of His self-sufficiency.

{4} {And there is none comparable to Him (kufuwan) — anyone}: neither in His names, nor in His attributes, nor in His acts; blessed and exalted is He.

This surah comprises the affirmation of the Oneness of the Names and Attributes (tawhid al-asma' wa'l-sifat).
